# How Much Does a Commercial Cost to Make? (2026)
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/how-much-does-a-commercial-cost/
By Zach Wennstedt. Updated 2026-11-06.

Short answer: making a 30-second TV commercial usually costs a few thousand dollars for a simple local spot and $50,000 or more for a national one, before you buy any airtime. One TV ad seller's 2026 guide puts local production at $3,000 to $15,000 and national at $50,000 to $500,000. Airtime is a separate bill.

Every top result for this question is written by someone selling production, and each one quotes its own range. We sell video too, so here's what we did differently: we put the numbers side by side, named where each one comes from, and dated them. Prices change, so check the sources before you sign anything.

## How much does it cost to make a 30-second commercial?

Here's how Simulmedia, a company that sells TV advertising, breaks down production costs in its guide (updated February 2026):

Production cost of a 30-second TV commercial, by type. Source: Simulmedia (a TV ad seller), 2026.
Type of commercial | Typical production cost | 

Local | $3,000 to $15,000 | 

Regional | $15,000 to $50,000 | 

National (standard) | $50,000 to $500,000 | 

Celebrity or premium | $500,000 to $1 million+ | 

Source: Simulmedia, "TV ad production costs" (https://www.simulmedia.com/blog/tv-ad-production-costs) (published May 2025, updated Feb 9, 2026). The guide doesn't say how the ranges were measured, so read them as one seller's estimate, not a survey.

The other production-company guides ranking for this question on November 6, 2026 landed in the same neighborhood: simple local spots in the low-to-mid thousands, polished national spots in the tens of thousands and up. Nobody in the business publishes a neutral, survey-based average, so be wary of anyone who sounds too precise.

## What makes a commercial cost more?

Commercials get expensive for the same reasons movies do: people and days. The big levers:

- Shoot days. Every day on set pays a crew, gear, insurance and food. One day versus three can be the whole difference between a local and a regional budget.

- Talent. Union actors, voice actors and anyone famous cost more, and some contracts pay again each time the ad runs.

- Locations and sets. Your shop is cheap. A closed street, a permit or a built set isn't.

- Music. Licensing a known song can cost more than the shoot. Original or library music is far cheaper.

- Revisions. Each round of changes after the shoot means more editing hours, and reshoots are the most expensive revision there is.

- Versions. A 30-second TV cut, a 15-second cut, and vertical cuts for TikTok and Reels are each extra work.

## How much does it cost to make a 1-minute commercial?

More than double a 30, usually, but not because of the minutes. A longer spot needs more scenes, more setups and more editing, so shoot days and post-production grow. If you only need the length for the web, ask for a 30-second version with a longer online cut made from the same shoot. That's often the cheapest way to get both.

## How much does it cost to air a commercial?

Airtime is billed on top of production, and it swings wildly by market and time of day. Simulmedia's same guide gives these local ranges for a 30-second spot:

Local TV airtime for one 30-second spot. Source: Simulmedia, 2026.
Market size (by DMA rank) | Cost per spot | 

Small markets (151 to 210) | $200 to $1,500 | 

Mid markets (51 to 150) | $500 to $3,000 | 

Large markets (1 to 50) | $2,000 to $10,000 | 

Top 10 markets | $5,000 to $50,000+ | 

At the very top end, CNBC reported that advertisers paid as much as $10 million for 30 seconds during Super Bowl LX in February 2026 (CNBC, Feb 10, 2026 (https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/02/10/nearly-125-million-watch-seahawks-crush-patriots-in-super-bowl-lx.html)).

Most small businesses don't start on TV at all. They run the same video as a social ad, where you set the daily budget yourself and can stop anytime.

## Is video worth it for a small business?

The best yearly numbers come from Wyzowl, a video company that has surveyed marketers and consumers for 12 years. Its 2026 report (266 respondents, surveyed late 2025) found:

- 91% of businesses use video as a marketing tool.

- 82% of video marketers say video gives them a good return on investment, down from 93% in 2025.

- 85% of people say a video has convinced them to buy something.

Source: Wyzowl, Video Marketing Statistics 2026 (https://wyzowl.com/video-marketing-statistics/). Wyzowl sells video production, so treat it as an industry survey, not independent research.

## What does an AI-made commercial cost?

AI changes the cost of the camera, not the cost of good ideas. Here's how pricing works at Madwackd Studio, with no crew day involved:

Option | Price | Best for | 

Make it yourself in the studio | Plans from $29/month (see pricing (https://www.madwackd.ai/pricing/)) | Short social ads and clips you direct yourself, with a price shown before every render | 

Done-for-you ad spot | From $2,500 | A finished spot planned, made and revised by a producer | 

Custom music video | From $5,000 | Artists and brands who want a full story, like the two in our Video Vault (https://www.madwackd.ai/vault/) | 

High-end commercial | Quoted, often $20,000 to $30,000+ | Multi-scene campaigns with many versions | 

An honest comparison: an AI clip is not the same thing as a crew-shot national spot with real actors on a real set. What it can do is let a small business test an idea for the price of lunch, then put real money behind the version that works. If you'd rather hand the whole thing off, our human producers (https://www.madwackd.ai/producers/) plan it with you.

## How to keep your commercial budget under control

- Write one sentence first: who it's for, the one thing you want them to do, and why now.

- Decide where it runs before you decide how it looks. A vertical social ad and a TV spot need different shoots.

- Get every price in writing up front, including revisions, music and extra cuts.

- Test small, then scale. Run two or three short versions on social and put the budget behind the winner.

- Plan where the clicks go. An ad that sends people to a slow or confusing page wastes the spend. Search Converts (https://searchconverts.com/?utm_source=madwackd&utm_medium=xpromo&utm_campaign=corner-commercial-cost), part of the Madwackd family, builds landing pages made to turn ad clicks into leads.

Not sure which option fits? Ask Madi, our AI producer (the chat button on every page). Tell her what you sell and your budget, and it will walk you through the options and prices. It's an AI, and it will tell you so.

# How to Make an AI Music Video: How We Made Ours
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/how-we-made-two-ai-music-videos/
By Zach Wennstedt. Updated 2026-11-06.

Short answer: you can make a music video with AI, but a good one isn't one prompt. Our two music videos, Tell Me Why (4:19) and What Love Really Is (5:01), each took an original song, a locked character design, dozens of AI shots, a frame-by-frame review, retakes, and many rounds of edits by a human producer.

Most guides for "how to make an AI music video for my song" say the same thing: upload your song, pick a style, press go. That gets you a video. It doesn't get you one people watch to the end. Here's what it actually took to make the two music videos in our Video Vault (https://www.madwackd.ai/vault/), written and produced by Zach Wennstedt, the founder of Madwackd Studio. We'll share the process and the lessons. The exact tools and prompts stay in the studio.

Tell Me Why, country music video, 4:19. Written and produced by Zach Wennstedt. A Madwackd Studio production.

## Step 1: Start with the song, then map every line

Both songs were written by Zach. Before making a single picture, we timed every sung line to a fraction of a second with speech-to-text. That timing sheet becomes the edit plan: which shot plays under which words, where the chorus lands, where a cut can hide.

## Step 2: Lock the look before you make shots

The number one problem with AI video is drift: the same character looks like a different person in the next shot. So we make a reference first and hold every shot to it.

- For Tell Me Why, the cowboy is Zach himself, made from his own photos with his consent. (We never make a real person's likeness without their OK. See our trust and safety (https://www.madwackd.ai/trust/) rules.)

- For What Love Really Is, we made a character sheet first: a blue neon crescent moon with a quiff and high-tops, and a pink neon star with a ponytail and boots. Every one of the 25 shots used that sheet as its guide.

## Step 3: Stills first, then motion

Every shot starts as a still picture we approve, then becomes an 8-second moving clip. Stills are cheap and fast to fix. Clips cost more, so you only animate a frame you already like. Tell Me Why used 34 approved stills and 36 clips, cut together in 43 edits.

## Step 4: Check every frame, and retake what's wrong

We sampled frames from every clip and wrote down what broke. Real examples from these two videos:

- A neon star kept turning into a human girl. The cause was one word in the shot description. Removing it fixed the shots.

- Characters doubled, merged into the signs behind them, or picked up readable text that wasn't supposed to be there.

- In the human version of What Love Really Is, the face slowly drifted younger and narrower as he walked toward the camera.

For the neon video, 10 of 25 shots were retaken. Five still glitched after two tries, so instead of forcing them we used their approved still pictures with a slow camera push-in. Viewers can't tell, and the video stays clean.

## Step 5: Know when to drop a feature

We tried AI lip-sync twice on Tell Me Why. It never looked right, so we cut every singing shot. The final video tells the story with looks, hands and horses instead. Sometimes the best fix is removing the thing that doesn't work.

What Love Really Is, neon cartoon music video, 5:01. Written and produced by Zach Wennstedt. A Madwackd Studio production.

## Step 6: Edit like a producer, not a generator

The edit is where these videos came alive, and it's all human judgment:

- Tiny timing fixes. One line in Tell Me Why came in about 3 seconds after the previous one and felt late. We made four test cuts (the original, and 0.5, 1 and 1.5 seconds sooner). Zach picked 0.5 seconds.

- Repeating the best part. The walking chorus was the strongest moment of What Love Really Is, so we brought it back near the end. Making those repeats sound natural took four rounds: we measured where the song's energy and rhythm matched, cut only on the beat, and moved the whispered line onto the first melody.

- Fixing what the viewer notices. A blemish on a close-up, two riders who touch hands for one second and let go (they now hold hands through every horse shot), a hand bent the wrong way. Small things, but they're what makes a video feel finished.

- A whole new look when the first one isn't right. What Love Really Is started as a live-action-style video. Zach wanted something more original, so it was rebuilt as a neon cartoon, and that's the version on our site.

## Step 7: Finish and credit it honestly

Both videos end with a title card: the song name, "Written and produced by Zach Wennstedt," and "A Madwackd Studio production." We don't say "made with one click," because they weren't.

## What this means if you want a music video

If you want… | Do this | 

A few short visual clips for your song's social posts | Make them yourself in the studio (https://www.madwackd.ai/studio/). You see the price before every render. | 

A full music video with characters that stay consistent, a story and a real edit | Hire a Madwackd producer (https://www.madwackd.ai/producers/). Custom music videos start at $5,000. | 

## Common questions

### Can I make an AI music video for my song for free?

You can make short clips with free tools, and many apps offer a free try. A full-length video with consistent characters takes many clips plus retakes, so expect to pay for generation time or for someone's hours. Watch for watermarks and check whether the free plan allows commercial use.

### How do I make an AI video of myself singing?

You need clear, well-lit photos of yourself and a tool that supports likeness with consent. Be ready for lip-sync to be the hardest part: it's where AI music videos most often look wrong. We dropped it entirely on Tell Me Why and told the story without singing shots.

### How long does an AI music video take?

The renders are quick. The review and editing aren't. A one-prompt video can take minutes; a video you're proud of takes many rounds of checking, retakes and edits, often over days.

### Do I have to say it was made with AI?

Platforms like TikTok and YouTube ask about AI-generated content when you upload. Answer honestly. Our AI disclosure (https://www.madwackd.ai/ai-disclosure/) page explains how we label videos.

Got a song? Tell Madi, our AI producer, about it (the chat button on every page). She'll ask a few questions and help you pick between making clips yourself and a full custom video.

# Video Ads for Small Business: A 7-Step Guide
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/video-ads-for-small-business/
By Zach Wennstedt. Updated 2026-11-06.

Short answer: a small-business video ad works best when it's short, hooks people in the first three seconds, makes one offer, and tells viewers exactly what to do next. TikTok's own guide recommends 21 to 34 seconds for most ads. You can make one with AI for far less than a film crew, then test a few versions before spending real money.

Most "video ads for small business" guides are template galleries. Templates are fine, but they skip the part that decides whether the ad pays off: what you say, in what order, and where the click goes. This guide is the producer's version, built on what the ad platforms themselves publish.

## Why video, and why now?

Video is now the default, not the extra. Wyzowl's 2026 survey found 91% of businesses use video in their marketing, and 41% of marketers paid for video ads this year, up from 36%. 63% of video marketers say they've used AI to make video, up from 51% a year earlier. (Wyzowl, 2026 (https://wyzowl.com/video-marketing-statistics/); Wyzowl is a video company, 266 respondents.)

Small businesses are adopting AI fast too, though the numbers depend on who's asking and how. The U.S. Census Bureau found 19.8% of U.S. businesses used AI in some business function as of May 3, 2026 (Census Bureau, May 2026 (https://census.gov/library/stories/2026/05/ai-use-businesses.html)). The U.S. Chamber of Commerce's 2026 small-business report says two-thirds of small businesses now use AI (U.S. Chamber, Oct 2026 (https://www.uschamber.com/technology/2026-empowering-small-business-report)). Different surveys, different definitions, same direction.

## How long should a small-business video ad be?

For TikTok, the platform says it "recommends 21-34 seconds for most ads" (TikTok for Business video advertising guide (https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en/guides/video-advertising-guide)). Marketers in Wyzowl's survey lean the same way: 71% say videos between 30 seconds and 2 minutes work best. Our advice: make a 20 to 30 second main cut, plus a 6 to 10 second version of just the hook and offer for retargeting.

## How to make a video ad for your small business, step by step

### 1. Pick one customer and one action

"Everyone" isn't a target. Write one sentence: "Homeowners in our area who need X should call us this week because Y." That sentence is your ad.

### 2. Hook them in the first three seconds

TikTok's guide puts it plainly: "Hook viewers in the first three seconds," and skip long intros and logo animations. Open on the problem, the result, or something surprising, not your logo.

### 3. Show, then say

Show the product, the before-and-after, or the moment of relief. Put captions on the screen, because plenty of people scroll with the sound off.

### 4. Make one offer and one call to action

"Book this week, get X" beats a list of everything you do. End with the exact action: call, book, or visit, and show it on screen.

### 5. Make three versions, not one

Change only the hook between versions. Run them side by side with a small daily budget, and move the money to the one that brings in leads, not just views.

### 6. Label AI content honestly

Ad platforms ask you to disclose realistic AI-generated content. On TikTok that's a setting in Ads Manager. Turn it on when it applies. Honest labels don't hurt a good ad, and hiding them can get one pulled.

### 7. Send the click somewhere that converts

A great ad that lands on a slow, confusing page wastes the budget. Make sure the page matches the ad's offer and loads fast on a phone. If you don't have a site that does that yet, Eye To Ad (https://eyetoad.com/?utm_source=madwackd&utm_medium=xpromo&utm_campaign=corner-small-business-ads), part of the Madwackd family, builds websites made to get local businesses found.

## A simple 25-second ad script you can copy

Time | What's on screen | What it says | 

0 to 3 s | The problem, up close | The question your customer is already asking themselves | 

3 to 12 s | You solving it | What you do, in one sentence | 

12 to 20 s | The result or proof | The real outcome (no made-up reviews or numbers) | 

20 to 25 s | Offer + how to act | "Book this week at…" with the phone number or web address on screen | 

## What does it cost to make a video ad with AI?

With Madwackd Studio you can make short ad clips yourself, on plans from $29 a month, and you see the price before anything renders, so there are no surprise bills. If you'd rather not do it yourself, a done-for-you spot starts at $2,500, planned and revised by a producer. Compare that with traditional production in our guide to how much a commercial costs (https://www.madwackd.ai/producers-corner/how-much-does-a-commercial-cost/). Full details are on the pricing page (https://www.madwackd.ai/pricing/).

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Logo first. Nobody stays for a logo animation. Put it at the end.

- Too many messages. One offer per ad. Make another ad for the next offer.

- Fake proof. Invented reviews and testimonials can break FTC rules. Use real customers, with their permission, or skip it.

- Judging too early. Give each version enough spend and days to collect real results before picking a winner.

- Counting views instead of customers. Track calls, bookings and form fills.

Want a script for your business? Ask Madi, our AI producer (the chat button on every page). Tell her what you sell and who you sell to, and it will help you plan your first ad. It's an AI, and it says so.

# Founder's vision: data centers that heat homes and feed people
URL: https://www.madwackd.ai/vision/

The vision, in one line: data centers that heat homes, grow food on their roofs to feed people, and get built with an Earth-first mindset that puts life and the environment before profits. That's our goal. It's not built yet. Here's why I think it can be, and what we're doing right now.

By Zach Wennstedt, founder of Madwackd Productions

## Why I care

I grew up in Boulder, Colorado, hugging trees and getting outside every chance I had. I still do. I have kids, and I think about the world they're going to live in every day.

I also build with AI. Madwackd Studio runs on it. So I can't pretend the computers behind it are free. They use real electricity and they make real heat. The International Energy Agency estimates data centers used about 415 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2024, around 1.5% of the world's total, and expects that to more than double to about 945 TWh by 2030 (IEA, Energy and AI, 2025 (https://www.iea.org/reports/energy-and-ai/executive-summary)).

Almost all of that electricity ends up as heat. Most of it gets blown into the sky. That's the part that drives me nuts, because people need heat. And that's where the idea starts.

## The vision

### 1. Data centers that heat homes

Picture a data center as the furnace for a neighborhood. The servers run, the heat goes into hot-water pipes, and the pipes warm homes, schools and pools. Families pay less to stay warm, and a city burns less coal and gas.

### 2. Gardens on the roof that feed people

Data centers have huge, flat, sunny roofs and a steady supply of warmth. That's a greenhouse waiting to happen. Grow vegetables up there year-round, even in a Colorado winter, and give them to the neighbors, food banks and schools nearby.

### 3. Earth-first from the first drawing

Build it so life and the environment come before profits. Pick the site so the heat has somewhere to go. Use clean power. Save water. Treat the neighborhood like a partner, not a parking lot.

## This is already starting (real examples)

I'm not making this up out of thin air. Parts of it are already working:

Where | What the data-center heat does | Source | 

Odense, Denmark | Heat recovered from Meta's data center goes into the city's district heating, for more than 12,000 homes (2023), running since late 2019. | Ramboll project page (https://www.ramboll.com/projects/energy/meta-surplus-heat-to-district-heating) | 

Tallaght, Dublin, Ireland | A council-owned heat network uses waste heat from a nearby Amazon data center. Operating since 2023, it heats public buildings and 133 apartments, saving an estimated 1,500 tonnes of CO2 a year. | FEDARENE case study (https://fedarene.org/best-practice/turning-data-centre-waste-heat-into-a-public-energy-asset-the-tallaght-district-heating-scheme/) | 

Paris, France | Equinix said in 2024 it would send heat from its PA10 data center to a new neighborhood and the Olympic Aquatic Centre. | Equinix newsroom (https://newsroom.equinix.com/2024-06-05-Help-Us-Heat-Our-Neighbors-Equinix-Makes-Data-Center-Heat-Available-to-Warm-Nearby-Buildings-and-Swimming-Pools) | 

Espoo, Finland (planned) | The city says waste heat from a planned Microsoft data center region will cover about 40% of Espoo's district heating needs in the future. | City of Espoo (https://www.espoo.fi/en/articles/using-waste-heat-new-data-center-cover-40-espoos-district-heating-needs) | 

Governments are pushing too. The EU's Energy Efficiency Directive says data centers over 1 megawatt must use their waste heat unless it isn't technically or economically feasible (Directive (EU) 2023/1791, Art. 26 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023L1791)). Germany's Energy Efficiency Act requires new data centers starting from July 1, 2026 to reuse at least 10% of their energy as heat, rising to 20% from July 2028 (EnEfG, German federal law (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/enefg/__11.html)).

What I haven't found yet is one place that does all three: heats homes, grows food on the roof, and was designed Earth-first from day one. That's the gap. That's the dream.

## What we're doing now (the honest part)

Madwackd is a small studio. We don't own a data center, and I won't pretend we do. Here's what's true today:

- Part of every purchase goes to carbon removal. We contribute 1.5% of our revenue to help advance permanent carbon removal, through Stripe Climate. More on our mission page (https://www.madwackd.ai/our-mission/).

- No wasted renders. Every render is priced before it starts and runs on prepaid credits, so nobody burns compute on surprise or abandoned jobs. That's good for your wallet and for the planet.

- Caps on runaway spending. Budget caps and daily limits stop generation from running away on its own.

## Where we're going

These are goals, not claims. As Madwackd grows, I want to:

- Choose computing partners that reuse their heat and run on clean power, wherever we have a real choice.

- Publish how much we've sent to carbon removal, in plain numbers.

- Make video for environmental and community groups so their stories get seen.

- Someday help build the real thing: a data center that keeps a neighborhood warm and feeds it from the roof.

Life and the environment before profits. That's our goal, and that's my vision. If you're working on any piece of this, a city, a builder, a grower, an engineer, I want to hear from you. Call us at 1-800-481-8638 (https://www.madwackd.aitel:+18004818638).

Zach WennstedtFounder, Madwackd Productions

# Custom Creator Studio: tell Genie what you make (https://www.madwackd.ai/custom-creator-studio/)

A personalized creator dashboard and AI production team built around one creator's channel, with every Madwackd studio tool inside and a human producer pass. Visitors type what they dream of making; the page itemizes the studio they would get (brand kit, content calendar, hook and caption starters, per-platform cutdowns and one-tap share, render credits, Producer Z with a voice, a published press release and a Creator Spotlight, a human producer pass), then they choose START (join the Founding Creator list) or THINK ABOUT IT (the plan is kept under their email).

## What is the Founding Creator offer?
$99 a month for the first 12 months, then the regular price (today $299 a month). Billed monthly, renews until cancelled, cancel anytime in one click, 14-day money-back on the first payment. Includes every studio tool, the personalized dashboard and production team, a human producer pass, 120 Fast render credits a month (about five 8-second clips; credit packs from $14), 3 Talking Z minutes, one published press release and a Creator Spotlight on madwackd.ai. It is a beta price: the full studio with a smaller render allowance and a direct line to a human producer. Founding rate for the first 100 founding creators or through November 22, 2026, whichever comes first.

## What is a credit, and what is a clip?
Credits pay for render time. A clip is one 8-second AI video shot. Every render shows its exact credit price before you confirm; technical failures are refunded automatically.

## Does it post to my socials for me?
Not yet. Today you cut, caption and export for TikTok, Reels, Shorts, YouTube, Instagram, X, LinkedIn and allofus.one from one panel and share with one tap. Direct posting rolls out platform by platform as each approves the Madwackd app.

## What does the human producer do?
A real producer reviews the dashboard within one business day: brand kit, tone, links and the plan, then approves or fixes it, and drafts the press release for the creator's approval.

## Who owns the work? Are AI clips labeled?
The creator owns their projects; every project comes with a rights pack. AI-generated clips carry an AI label.

## Other tiers
Free Creator Studio tools ($0); Starter $29 and Pro $89 plans; Custom Creator Studio (Studio tier, $299 regular); Genie Production Team $499 (4,800 credits, 3 brand kits, same-day producer pass plus a monthly 30-minute call); done-for-you production from $2,500.
